proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10648 raśmi “rope” gives Prakrit rassi/rāsi and Punjabi rassī, explicitly transmitted to Hindi and several other IA languages. Under the user’s policy this family is linked while the survey lect’s immediate transmission remains unresolved; no uninterrupted inheritance is asserted.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10286 mṛttikā gives Pali mattikā, Prakrit maṭṭī/mittiā, Punjabi/Hindi miṭṭī and eastern māṭi “earth, clay”; its Kachchi addendum explicitly includes “dust”. Clay/earth used for mud is the same material family, with local transmission left open.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 13355 sāra explicitly gives Lahnda/Punjabi sārā, Marwari sāro, Gujarati sārũ and Marathi sārā “all, whole”. The article argues for development from “best part”, while recording the competing older account; regional borrowing remains possible.
